steps.content: Hecate can't remember how many times she blacks out. Now, struggling to open her eyes, she realizes she is wavering in a small alley of the shifting maze.

The maze morphs relentlessly, growing and spreading, as if it is alive, determined to imprison her. Shackles jut from her body, plunging her thoughts into chaos, making her feel as if she is staggering on the crest of raging ocean waves.
...Wait, it's not what she thought. Someone's carrying her, an old, bent man struggling to escape the maze with her on his back.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...The Black Ring's coming to life, worsening the contamination inside you. But don't worry now, just rest for a bit.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Got the White Cube. Hang onto it; it'll help you feel better.
She feels a soothing sensation at her chest. Glancing down, she realizes she is clutching something against it—a bizarre, white box.
Around the White Cube, the contamination gently streams into it, settling down once it is absorbed.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: This is the thing that can save Chief... You've met that person, haven't you? You know Chief's location now, don't you?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Then... quick, let's go back... I need to—oof!
She makes a brief attempt to move, causing Samuel to stagger, barely keeping himself from hitting the ground.
Hecate only then realizes, the man's stooped back is deeply stained with contamination. Had he gotten it from carrying her? Her mind reels.
This seems all too familiar. Who had been left behind last time, sacrificing themselves to protect her when she blindly rushed ahead, deceived by Mania? Was Hella awake yet?
Why would you do so much for someone who's a mere stranger to you?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Why... Were you given an order? Did Donald tell you to look out for me?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Why else would anyone go this far...
Beneath the Black Ring, for the first time, she can label her feelings: a seething hatred with nowhere to be released.
It is only now that she really understands the true target of her hatred.
It isn't Rustfire she hates; it is herself, for feeling so powerless without Chief, like she can't do anything on her own.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Don't overthink it; it's just the Black Ring messing with your mind. No one gave me that kind of order; I choose to do this.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Please, stop... My only concern is Chief, just following orders. That's not your job! Don't do this for me... I don't get it, and I don't need to...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I can't take it anymore... Put me down, you can move faster alone... Hurry, go...
The roaring of the Corruptors is getting closer. The camouflage sorcery is broken; they have no means left to conceal themselves. Samuel quickly realizes that the two of them can't possibly get far.
After a brief silence, he finds a corner to place Hecate down, averting his eyes, his voice wavering slightly as he speaks.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Don't be hard on yourself, Hecate. You haven't done anything wrong. Ever since I led you into this maze, I made a promise to get you out alive. All of this... it's for me, really.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: I wanted to bring you back with me to make amends for past regrets. I can't bear the thought of repeating my old mistakes. This was all my choice.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: You've done nothing wrong. You've always stuck to your goals, fighting and not giving up, even when you were battered and scarred... If I were you, I'd be proud of myself.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: The real cowards... are those who flee from their own fights.
His head droops even lower, his speech growing more labored.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: The worst kind of mistakes... are those you can't confess, have no one to apologize to, and can never make up for.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: On your journey, there's still a lot you can accomplish.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: ...Stop talking like that, it's beyond me, and I don't need it...

Clasping Hecate's hand, he encourages her to hold on firmly to the White Cube and the last dose of the sedative. With the Corruptors' howls closing in, the old man finally finds the bravery to gaze into the girl's eyes.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: I'm leaving now. You stay here for a while, take a moment to calm yourself, and look for the right moment to make your move. The exit is close by.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Be extra careful when you are on your own. Make it out alive and return safely to the ones who matter the most to you.

The man leaves Hecate, confused and alone, hidden in a narrow gap. He ventures out, walking far enough to be seen. In a corner in the Corruptors' line of sight, he knocks on the wall, attracting their attention.
If he could just lure them away, she'd be out of danger. She'd definitely find her way back, back to her loved ones.
...Can this act lighten his burden of sin?
The Corruptors, engulfed in contamination, rush at the old man. Their howls shake his tainted mind, awakening a flood of past, dark misdeeds.
[Entering Memory]

steps.speaker: Chaotic Memory
steps.content: ...He is one of the W-31 survivors... wait, no, deserters...

steps.speaker: Chaotic Memory
steps.content: You stood by as heroes fell, escaping by yourself... How can you show your face here again...

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Really... Sophie bravely fought to the end, never fleeing. She died a hero, a heroic death...

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: So you ran back here... You survived just to break the news of my daughter's death?
[Exit Memory]

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: It's fine, this was long overdue... I should have died... 9 years ago...

He reassures himself, but terror fractures his mind. The maze turns into a trap, with the Corruptors closing in from everywhere, their hands groping through the slim cracks. Samuel collapses, scrabbling on the ground.
He is always the coward, with both humiliating memories and base instincts resurfacing in death's presence.

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: It's terrifying... This place, it's terrifying...

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: How did we end up like this? I thought we had won the negotiations. Didn't we secure our mines? Weren't we full of hope?

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: Why was everyone dead? Why are they all monsters now? It wasn't supposed to be like this; nobody saw this coming.

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: No one thought they would die here. If we had any idea about this—

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Shut up, I need to stop being a coward, no more regrets, this is the last chance.

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: It's terrifying... We are just normal people, not Sinners, not powerful, not brave.

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: I'm sorry, but I don't want to die. I need to go back, I need to see her again. I don't want to die here.

steps.speaker: Young Samuel
steps.content: Please, hero, save me...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: ...I've got this, you're not going to die on my watch.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Enough with the guilt. You went in the mine because you trusted me, and I definitely can't disappoint you now.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I'll get us back, all of us. I promise to bring every single one of us back safely.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: If it hadn't been for people like me... He wouldn't have ended up—

steps.speaker: Corruptor
steps.content: Roarrrr!!!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: No—!!

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Ah...

In the nick of time, before the monsters shred him to pieces, the exhausted Nightmare stops all the attacks. Hecate, propped against the wall, wears a look of agony and bewilderment, clearly at a loss as to why she would do such a thing.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Please, no more of this; stop being so nice to me. I'm here to finish the job, that's it. I—

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I'm too weak, I failed to even keep Chief safe. So don't make me care about anyone else!

Death's shadow hasn't lifted yet. Hecate, in her current state, can't rescue anyone. She's weak, but she managed to give Samuel a brief respite, enough for him to understand his own heart before blacking out.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: It's disgraceful, yet here I am, still clinging to life...
Holding out hope... that a hero shows up...
[Pikachu Lightning]—Time to flaunt some dazzling effects.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Good heavens, what on earth happened to you two?!
He rummages in a flurry to administer sedatives to both, mumbling complaints under his breath all the while.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Didn't I tell you not to push yourself? Hey, FAC bro!! Over here!! Over here!!

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Quick, get these two back to safety, please—I owe you, like ten huge favors!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: That just now... was that your power?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I was right, you're a Sinner... an incredibly strong one at that... Donald, you must be able to do anything...
Her hands quiver as she hands the White Cube to Donald.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Deliver this... to Chief... save him...
steps.female_content: Deliver this... to Chief... save her...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I'm just not fast enough... not strong enough... The things I can't manage, I'm begging you, please take over...

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Sigh... I was this close to saying yes. I'm really sorry, Hecate.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: I'd love to be the hero here, but I just can't pull it off this time. We've got something on our tail, and if I don't hold the fort, nobody's getting out of here.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: That's why I'm counting on you this time.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: The rescue of Chief is in your hands. You've got to find the person who's most important to you. I can't say much here, but I hope that shackle leads you where you need to go.
He hands the White Cube back to Hecate and gives her shoulder a reassuring pat.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Stop selling yourself short, and forget about needing "someone stronger." You're strong in your own right, and there's plenty out there ready to back you up. You've never been the underdog.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Go and chase down your dreams by any means necessary. It's up to you now.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: In return, I'll block all the tailgaters here, making sure you've got a clear run.

The maze grows and twists, falling apart at seams, with the Corruptors swarming out like a flood, beyond any containment. FAC soldiers prop up their injured, casting a last look at the Executive Officer.

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: ...We're heading out, back to the defense line. Remember our deal, you will come back, and don't forget to bring ${PlayerName} along.
Without a word or a backward glance, Donald faces the approaching monster wave. He just lifts his left hand in a casual wave, his fingertips sparking with electricity.
He must really believe he's got style doing that.
